problem: The daily filings have buried him
action: Inside the office, mid-morning. The dealer sits at his desk with a thick untidy stack of loose paper forms in front of him, some spilling sideways. His elbow is on the desk and his forehead rests in his open hand, fingers pushed up into his hair. His eyes are closed or nearly closed. A pen lies where he dropped it.
lighting: Hard window light from the left striking the white paper so the stack is the brightest thing in the frame and glares slightly; his face is in the softer shadow beside it.
camera: Chest-up from across the desk, slightly low, the paper stack occupying the lower third of the vertical frame and his head and hand the upper half. 35mm.
detail: CRITICAL — every sheet is BLANK white paper. No printing, no forms, no boxes, no ruling, no writing, no letters, no numbers, no logos on any sheet. Same cream full-sleeve shirt with the sleeves rolled, same dark navy trousers, same watch.
feeling: Buried. Not by one hard thing but by twenty small ones, every single day.
motion: His hand slides a fraction further up his forehead. He exhales. A very slow push in. Nothing else moves, no cuts, no camera shake, nobody speaks.

voice_over.hi: सेफ़्टी डिक्लेरेशन, वॉटर टेस्टिंग, मिनिमम वेज, स्वच्छता, वर्क परमिट — रोज़। तो पंप कब चलाएँ?
